summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — OR.PA +6%, BP.L +4%, TTE.PA +4%, ITH.L +4%, SHELL.AS +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (KER.PA -17%, SAF.PA -10%, BESI.AS -8%, RR.L -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: KER.PA (-16.57%) — Q3 update (reported Fri 23 Oct): Gucci comparable sales -6%, group -1%, with weaker China/Japan traffic. Shares fell ~16%, their worst day ever, and EU luxury hit decade lows. Likely the same move, dated late. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: KER.PA is a Paris-listed large-cap luxury name that no strategy includes. It was also a results-day gap-down, and a long-only bot cannot short it or fade it, and it had no pre-market signal.

top_movers.catalyst: No same-day news found. Likely L'Oréal's Q3 sales release, which usually lands in late October, but I couldn't confirm it. A beat would fit a +5.6% move after strong Q1 and H1 2026 growth.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: OR.PA is a large-cap (~€230B) Euronext Paris consumer staples/beauty name that no strategy covers. If the move was a results-day gap, a gap-up or RSI filter would also have excluded it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap CAC40/Euro Stoxx 50 staples and luxury names (e.g. OR.PA, MC.PA, RMS.PA) to the news-reactive universe, with a post-earnings gap rule such as gap ≥ +4% on ≥1.5× average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst for a +4.35% move. Press reports for 26 Oct 2026 show BP down 1–2% (about 629p) as Brent eased on US–Iran de-escalation hopes, which contradicts the bot's figure. Likely a data or close-price artifact.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BP.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap oil major that no strategy covers. A +4.35% close-to-close move that isn't visible in intraday reports also suggests a bad close or stale prior close, which a price-sanity filter would reject.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a data-quality check that cross-checks close-to-close moves against a second source (or the prior-day close) before flagging a mover. Separately, consider adding FTSE 100 energy names to a commodity-linked universe.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found; likely a sector-wide move in European energy/oil stocks, consistent with oil prices responding to the US-Iran conflict. The driver is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: TTE.PA is a Euronext Paris large-cap (~€165-177bn) oil major, and no strategy covers it. A sector-driven, newsless +4.3% gap also gives news-reactive filters nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap Euronext energy names (TTE.PA, SHEL, BP, ENI) to the momentum universe, plus a sector-breadth trigger that enters when ≥3 energy names gap up ≥3% with Brent confirming.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for Ithaca Energy (UK North Sea oil & gas) on 2026-10-26; searches returned nothing dated today. Likely an energy-sector or commodity-price move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ITH.L is a UK mid-cap E&P (FTSE 250 range) and no strategy's universe includes it. A +3.87% move with no news is also too small and undirected for gap-up or news-reactive triggers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add UK/EU oil & gas mid-caps (ITH.L, plus peers like HBR.L and EnQuest) to the commodity/energy strategy universe. Gate entry on a sector-relative strength rule, e.g. the name beats its sector ETF by ≥2% on volume ≥1.2× the 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-26 — likely an oil/energy sector-driven move. A search turned up no Shell-specific news for that date.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SHELL.AS is a large-cap Amsterdam-listed energy major, a secondary listing of the London-primary Shell. No strategy covers it, so no momentum or news filter ever evaluated it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add SHELL.AS (or Shell's primary London line) to the uk-eu momentum universe, and add a sector-relative screen that flags large-cap energy names with a daily move of at least +3% on above-average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst. Searches found no Shell-specific news for 2026-10-26. Midday reports I found showed Shell down ~1-2% with Brent near $114, which contradicts the +3.72% close, so the move is unexplained.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SHEL.L is a FTSE 100 mega-cap integrated oil major, and no strategy lists it. A late-session reversal with no news would also not have passed gap-up or volume-spike entry filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap energy (SHEL.L, BP.L) to the uk-eu momentum universe, with a Brent-linked sector-momentum gate. Also verify the +3.72% and 40.33 close against a second price source, since they conflict with the intraday reports.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 update (reported Fri 23 Oct): Gucci comparable sales -6%, group -1%, with weaker China/Japan traffic. Shares fell ~16%, their worst day ever, and EU luxury hit decade lows. Likely the same move, dated late.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: KER.PA is a Paris-listed large-cap luxury name that no strategy includes. It was also a results-day gap-down, and a long-only bot cannot short it or fade it, and it had no pre-market signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add KER.PA, MC.PA and RMS.PA to a long-only mean-reversion universe, entering only after a ≥12% single-day drop on a sector-wide selloff with RSI(2)<10 and a 1-day confirmation close. Also check the 1-3 day timestamp lag on mover data.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed news catalyst found for 2026-10-26. Searches show only a slide to ~€310 before the Oct 23 Q3 revenue release, and nothing reporting the -10% move; possibly a delayed Q3 reaction or sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SAF.PA is a large-cap (~€110B+) French aerospace/defence name that no strategy includes. A one-day -10% gap on a stock with no news in the feed would also trip gap/volatility filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap CAC 40/Stoxx 50 constituents to the mean-reversion strategy's universe, gated by a gap-down ≥8% rule and a no-negative-guidance check, so the next large-cap flush is evaluated rather than ignored.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-26; likely a sector-wide semicap/AI-chip equipment sell-off or profit-taking after a volatile autumn (shares were ~€192-222 in Aug, €145 now).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BESI is a mid/large-cap Dutch semiconductor-equipment name on Euronext Amsterdam, and no strategy's universe includes it. The bot is also likely long-only, so it can't act on a drop.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EU semicap names (BESI.AS, ASM International, ASML) to the uk-eu momentum/mean-reversion universe, with a sector-correlation filter to flag a -5% or worse sector-wide down day.

top_movers.catalyst: Safran warned of softening wide-body jet aftermarket demand (GE Aerospace also flagged softness), hitting engine peers. RR.L fell to about 1,164p, a multi-month low. Search dated the drop to 23 Oct, so the timing is uncertain.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: RR.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap aerospace/defence name that no strategy covers. The drop was a peer-read-through gap on a sector warning, so any momentum or news filter would also have seen it only after the open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 aerospace names (RR.L, BA.L) to the uk-eu news-reactive universe. Add a peer-warning trigger that flags a sector basket when a major peer (Safran, GE) issues a downgrade or profit warning and the name gaps down ≥4%.
